subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — core event contracts

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-event AI-safety taxonomy and its plugin emission model as a permanent core and Plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The event names, privacy fields, versioning semantics, trusted provenance, and plugin authorization model become durable operator and third-party contracts; code review cannot choose those policies without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed contract
options.body: Approve the direction after the trusted-emitter bypass is removed, every event carries a schema version, and the SDK and privacy contract is documented.

options.title: Keep it internal first
options.body: Land an internal-only experimental taxonomy without public Plugin SDK exports, then promote a stabilized contract in a later reviewed change.

options.title: Defer the taxonomy
options.body: Pause or close the four-PR series until a maintainer-sponsored design establishes concrete emitters, consumers, privacy rules, and ownership.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed contract
recommendation.body: Approve the direction after the trusted-emitter bypass is removed, every event carries a schema version, and the SDK and privacy contract is documented.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core product scope and a new permanent public SDK contract, while the feature history traces back to their diagnostics architecture work.
